name: Signature header declares label 'sig1' twice (malformed structured dictionary)
spec_reference: #verifier-checklist-requests step 1 (RFC 9421 §4.2 Signature is a Dictionary; RFC 8941 §3.2 keys are unique; AdCP rejects duplicate labels rather than retaining the last)
$comment: RFC 9421 §4.2 defines the Signature field as a Dictionary, and RFC 8941 §3.2 makes dictionary keys unique, and a standard parser (RFC 8941 §4.2.2) resolves a duplicate by silently overwriting with the last value. That overwrite is the ambiguity: AdCP step 1 therefore treats a repeated label as malformed, the same downgrade-protection posture as 021, and verifiers MUST reject rather than retain the last value. Signature-Input carries sig1 exactly once and is well formed; only the Signature header repeats the label. Accepting it lets two parties disagree on which signature bytes belong to sig1 — one verifies the first, another reads the last — over a Signature-Input both agree on. Same rule as 021-duplicate-signature-input-label, applied to the other signature header. Both values are well-formed 64-byte sf-binary placeholders, so a verifier that rejects only on an unparseable signature will not reject here.
